title: REMOTE HOST IDENTIFICATION HAS CHANGED
role: You own the CI runners and deploy servers that pull code from GitHub over SSH.

source.label: GitHub: we updated our RSA SSH host key (24 March 2023)

brief: Friday morning, 24 March 2023. Every deploy job that runs `git fetch` over SSH has failed since about 05:00 UTC. Builds that use HTTPS are fine. Sam has a fix ready: turn off host key checking in CI.

steps.situation: This is the error from a deploy runner.
steps.evidence:
$ git fetch origin
@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@
@    WARNING: REMOTE HOST IDENTIFICATION HAS CHANGED!     @
@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@
IT IS POSSIBLE THAT SOMEONE IS DOING SOMETHING NASTY!
The fingerprint for the RSA key sent by the remote host is
SHA256:(a fingerprint you have never seen).
Offending RSA key in /var/lib/deploy/.ssh/known_hosts:3
Host key verification failed.

choices.text: Treat it as a possible attack until GitHub's official channels explain it
choices.why: A changed host key means either the server's key was rotated or someone sits in the middle. GitHub's blog and status page said which: the RSA key had been replaced.

choices.text: Set StrictHostKeyChecking no in the CI SSH config
choices.why: Builds go green, but you've switched off the only check that would catch a real man-in-the-middle, at the very moment a key is in question.

choices.text: Delete known_hosts on every runner and accept whatever key comes
choices.why: You trust the first key you see without checking it, and you lose every other pinned host as well.

steps.situation: GitHub says its RSA private key was briefly exposed in a public repository. It replaced the key at about 05:00 UTC and published the new one. ECDSA and Ed25519 keys did not change.
steps.evidence:
$ ssh-keygen -R github.com
# Host github.com found: line 3
/var/lib/deploy/.ssh/known_hosts updated.
$ curl -sL https://api.github.com/meta | jq -r '.ssh_keys[]' | sed 's/^/github.com /' >> ~/.ssh/known_hosts
$ ssh-keygen -lf ~/.ssh/known_hosts | grep github.com

choices.text: Remove the old entry, add keys from GitHub's API over HTTPS, compare the fingerprint with the blog
choices.why: That's GitHub's documented fix. The key comes over a channel you can verify (HTTPS), and you check the fingerprint against a second source.

choices.text: ssh once by hand and type yes
choices.why: Usually fine, but you're trusting the key the network gave you instead of one you checked.

choices.text: Switch all deploys to HTTPS with a personal token
choices.why: A rushed change to every pipeline, and one person's long-lived token becomes a shared deploy secret.

steps.situation: Two runners are fixed. Where else is the old key pinned?

choices.text: Search config management, runner images and base images for the old key; fix it there and redeploy
choices.why: Hand fixes are lost on the next rebuild. GitHub also warned that workflows using `actions/checkout` pinned to a commit with `ssh-key` needed an update.

choices.text: Fix each server by hand when it fails
choices.why: Failures keep coming for weeks, each one a fresh puzzle for whoever is on call.

choices.text: Switch all hosts to ignore RSA and use Ed25519 only, today
choices.why: A good long-term move, but changing key types across the fleet mid-incident adds risk. Plan it for after.

steps.situation: In the review someone asks: what would we do if *our* private key leaked into a public repo?

choices.text: Rotate at once, publish the new fingerprint, tell users what to do, and add secret scanning to every push
choices.why: GitHub had no evidence of abuse and rotated anyway, out of caution. Once a key is public you can't know who copied it.

choices.text: Delete the commit, force-push and hope nobody saw it
choices.why: Bots scrape public pushes within minutes, and forks and caches keep copies. The key is burned the moment it's pushed.
Users then see a scary warning with no explanation, and some will turn off checking to make it go away.

debrief.what_happened: On 24 March 2023 GitHub replaced the RSA SSH host key for github.com at about 05:00 UTC, after the private key was briefly exposed in a public GitHub repository. GitHub said it had no reason to believe the key was abused and acted out of caution. Only RSA was affected: ECDSA and Ed25519 host keys, HTTPS Git and web traffic were unchanged. Clients that had pinned the old RSA key saw the host-key-changed warning. GitHub's fix was to run `ssh-keygen -R github.com` and add the new key, either from the post or from `api.github.com/meta`, then check the published fingerprint. Workflows pinning `actions/checkout` to a commit SHA with `ssh-key` needed updating.
lessons: A host key warning is a security signal: verify out of band, never disable checking.
Pin known_hosts through config management so rotations are one change.
A leaked private key is burned: rotate at once and tell users how to verify.
Scan every push for secrets before it reaches a public repo.
